narrative:
The decision to deny your law school application was primarily influenced by a prediction indicating an 84.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam if you were to take it. This high probability suggests that, based on the data from previous students, your profile aligns more closely with those who did not succeed on their first attempt.

The most significant factors contributing to this prediction were your academic performance in your first and third years, which placed you in the lowest decile compared to your peers. While the average for accepted students in their first year is around 6.00, your ranking was at 1.00, indicating that your grades were considerably lower than those of successful applicants. Similarly, your third-year performance also fell into the lowest decile, further reinforcing concerns about your readiness for the bar exam.

In contrast, your LSAT score, which was above average at 40.00, had a positive influence on the prediction, suggesting that you possess the potential to succeed. However, this was not enough to outweigh the concerns raised by your academic rankings. 

Given this feedback, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your academic performance, particularly in your remaining studies, and consider retaking the LSAT if you believe you can achieve a higher score. Strengthening your overall academic profile could enhance your chances of future acceptance into law school.
